newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells listed firms not to falsify figures.
newsitem.headline: China tells listed firms not to falsify figures.

text.p: The mouthpiece of China's ruling Communist Party warned listed companies on Wednesday not to falsify their financial statements, speculate in their own shares and issue false news.
The People's Daily, in a front-page article, warned listed companies not to falsify financial statements to cover up losses or to issue news that could affect share prices.
"Some listed companies create false financial statements to cover up losses," the newspaper said, adding that some exaggerate their assets and profits to boost share prices.
"This misleads vast numbers of small and medium-sized investors," it said.
Some listed firms pour capital into the stock market and speculate in their own shares, the newspaper said.
The People's Daily also warned against the listing of lumbering state enterprises just to keep them afloat, saying this deviated from the basic principle of listing companies.
Funds raised from listings are sometimes used without conducting feasibility studies, the newspaper said.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission has been prudent when reviewing and approving applications for listing and has punished companies seeking listings, underwriters and law firms that falsify figures, it said.
Some share prices are overstated, the newspaper said.
The newspaper said the authorities should slap heavier fines on violators.
It suggested that securities regulators hire experts to review applications for listings to ensure the review process is scientific and fair.
The public should be encouraged to tip off securities regulators about irregularities, it said.
Too many unqualified companies were seeking to list, it said. "The temperature of listings is soaring blindly," the newspaper said.
